limitations_and_boundaries: The study uses a mouse model of LPS-induced neuroinflammation; generalizability to other neuroinflammatory conditions or species is not established.
C1q neutralization was achieved by antibody administration; genetic knockout or pharmacological inhibition approaches were not tested.
The causal chain from C1q upregulation to microglial phagocytosis and synaptic loss is inferred from rescue experiments; direct demonstration of C1q binding to synapses was not performed.
Behavioral tests were limited to open field, Y-maze, and novel object recognition; other cognitive domains were not assessed.
Electrophysiological recordings were performed in anesthetized or ex vivo preparations, which may not fully reflect in vivo synaptic dynamics.
The study did not examine the role of other complement components or downstream effectors.
Sample sizes for some experiments (e.g., n=5 for dendritic spine analysis) are relatively small.
The LPS protocol used a single serotype and dose; dose-response and serotype effects were not explored.
